- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 2-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.53) and price is rising, model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought overcorrection.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon: if forecast exceeds 3σ above recent 10-day mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- In 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or rising.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low (e.g., 0.80 → 0.27 → 0.80), model misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3 days to anchor forecast.
